senate.description: Small modular reactors in Minnesota viability report appropriation

Senate.text: Referred to Environment, Climate, and Legacy

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to environment; appropriating money for a report on the viability of small modular reactors in Minnesota; requiring a report.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. [+APPROPRIATION; SMALL MODULAR REACTOR VIABILITY REPORT. +]

[+(a) $500,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency for a report on the viability and suitability of electricity supplied by small modular nuclear reactors in this state. By January 15, 2026, the commissioner, in consultation with the Environmental Quality Board, the Public Utilities Commission, the commissioner of natural resources, the commissioner of health, and the Critical Materials Recovery Advisory Task Force, must submit the report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over energy finance and policy, environment and natural resources finance and policy, health finance and policy, and capital investment. The report must include: +]

[+(1) recommendations for enhanced environmental monitoring and protection, including recommendations related to: +]

[+(i) water quality monitoring and standards that exceed federal requirements; +]

[+(ii) waste storage and management protocols that meet or exceed current federal and state requirements; +]

[+(iii) water appropriation, consumption, and recycling requirements; +]

[+(iv) environmental justice considerations; +]

[+(v) integration with and enhancement of existing environmental regulations; and +]

[+(vi) comprehensive ecosystem protection measures; +]

[+(2) recommendations for infrastructure and operational requirements, including: +]

[+(i) grid integration requirements and associated costs; +]

[+(ii) necessary regulatory framework adaptations; +]

[+(iii) emergency response infrastructure needs; +]

[+(iv) public health monitoring systems and requirements; +]

[+(v) baseline health assessment protocols; +]

[+(vi) long-term health surveillance infrastructure; and +]

[+(vii) health care workforce development needs; +]

[+(3) an assessment of the economic viability of deploying small modular reactors in this state, including an assessment of: +]

[+(i) power purchase agreement structures, including public-private partnerships; +]

[+(ii) rate impacts across customer classes; +]

[+(iii) economic impacts on existing utilities and communities; +]

[+(iv) revenue generation potential and projections; and +]

[+(v) community benefit and ownership models; and +]

[+(4) options for community engagement and benefit structures, including: +]

[+(i) cooperative ownership models; +]

[+(ii) revenue-sharing mechanisms; +]

[+(iii) local business protection measures; and +]

[+(iv) rural development opportunities. +]

[+(b) The report required by this section must include recommendations for any legislation needed to implement the identified requirements and strategies. The recommendations in the report must be specific and actionable and may not include recommendations for further reports or studies. +]

(a) $500,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency for a report on the viability and suitability of electricity supplied by small modular nuclear reactors in this state. By January 15, 2026, the commissioner, in consultation with the Environmental Quality Board, the Public Utilities Commission, the commissioner of natural resources, the commissioner of health, and the Critical Materials Recovery Advisory Task Force, must submit the report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over energy finance and policy, environment and natural resources finance and policy, health finance and policy, and capital investment. The report must include:
(1) recommendations for enhanced environmental monitoring and protection, including recommendations related to:
(i) water quality monitoring and standards that exceed federal requirements;
(ii) waste storage and management protocols that meet or exceed current federal and state requirements;
(iii) water appropriation, consumption, and recycling requirements;
(iv) environmental justice considerations;
(v) integration with and enhancement of existing environmental regulations; and
(vi) comprehensive ecosystem protection measures;
(2) recommendations for infrastructure and operational requirements, including:
(i) grid integration requirements and associated costs;
(ii) necessary regulatory framework adaptations;
(iii) emergency response infrastructure needs;
(iv) public health monitoring systems and requirements;
(v) baseline health assessment protocols;
(vi) long-term health surveillance infrastructure; and
(vii) health care workforce development needs;
(3) an assessment of the economic viability of deploying small modular reactors in this state, including an assessment of:
(i) power purchase agreement structures, including public-private partnerships;
(ii) rate impacts across customer classes;
(iii) economic impacts on existing utilities and communities;
(iv) revenue generation potential and projections; and
(v) community benefit and ownership models; and
(4) options for community engagement and benefit structures, including:
(i) cooperative ownership models;
(ii) revenue-sharing mechanisms;
(iii) local business protection measures; and
(iv) rural development opportunities.

(b) The report required by this section must include recommendations for any legislation needed to implement the identified requirements and strategies. The recommendations in the report must be specific and actionable and may not include recommendations for further reports or studies.
